title: Prompt Studio for non-developers — scratchpad
content:
Goal: sketch an MVP for a lightweight Prompt Studio aimed at non-developers (PMs, CS, content ops) so they can iterate on prompts, test model variants, and publish safe, versioned prompt templates into the Redwood Console without relying on eng.

Problem statement:
- PMs and CS regularly need to tune prompts for new features but wait on eng for integration and tuning windows.
- Current workflows: ad-hoc docs + tickets + manual PRs. Long feedback loop, lost iterations, drift.
- Non-dev folks fear messing with cost/latency or creating toxic responses; need guardrails and visibility.

MVP hypothesis:
- If we provide a simple web UI to compose prompts, run quick A/B trials against target models, and publish templates with RBAC and safety checks, non-dev teams will iterate 4x faster and reduce ticket churn by 30% within 3 months.

Success metrics (measurable):
- Adoption: 20 active template authors org-wide in month 1 of pilot.
- Time-to-publish: median time from first draft -> published template reduces from 7 days to <24 hours for pilot customers.
- Safety/quality: <1% published templates flagged for safety violations during first 500 publishes.
- Cost impact: average token cost change per template visible; authors see cost estimate before publish.

Core features (MVP scope):
1) Template editor (rich text w/ placeholders): name, description, example inputs, variable placeholders with types (string, enum, json).
2) Live test pane: run a prompt with sample inputs against 2 model variants (fast vs high-quality) and see side-by-side outputs. Toggle streaming vs non-streaming.
3) Token & cost estimator: rough token estimate + per-request cost estimate based on selected model and temperature.
4) Safety checks: built-in classifier run on outputs during test, warn if flagged; pre-publish scan of template and examples for PII / disallowed content heuristics.
5) Versioning & rollback: simple version history and ability to unpublish.
6) Publish to Console route: create a route (or link template) that engineers can wire; optional self-serve if RBAC allows.
7) Permissions: draft/publish permissions, owner, reviewers; audit log entry on publish.
8) Quick AB test toggle: publish as variant A/B for a route (for early rollout).

Nice-to-have (later):
- Guided prompt improvements (score-based suggestions) using internal eval harness.
- Template marketplace across org with rating & usage stats.
- Built-in evals tied to a small goldset for regressions.
- Bulk import from docx / CSV of existing prompts.

User stories (rough):
- As a PM, I want to author a prompt template with placeholders so that my product can inject customer context without exposing raw data.
- As a CS lead, I want to test a recovery prompt for escalations and preview outputs with the safety classifier so I can sign off before publish.
- As an engineer, I want to link a published template to a route in Console so the runtime uses the canonical prompt with minimal code changes.
- As an auditor, I want an exportable audit trail of publishes/rollbacks for compliance reviews.

Acceptance criteria (example):
- Editor autosaves drafts every 10s.
- Test pane returns results within 3s for small inputs on fast model (simulated local latency).
- Publishing requires at least one example input & output and a safety scan pass or explicit reviewer override.

Technical constraints & integrations:
- Must use existing Console auth & RBAC (no separate account system).
- Use Redwood API to run test calls (hosted token-limited sandbox); rate-limits enforced for non-dev users.
- Safety checks leverage existing safety microservice (calls to /safety/scan).
- Persist templates in internal metadata store (existing config DB) with lightweight schema: id, name, owner, body, placeholders[], examples[], versions[].
- Versioning model: simple revision number with diff view (text only).

UI sketch (very rough):
- Left column: template list + search + tags; center: editor; right: test pane + model selector + cost estimate + safety flags; top-right: publish button + version dropdown.

Rollout plan (pilot):
- Week 0–2: prototype UI mock + basic editor wired to hosted sandbox (no publish). Get 3 PMs + 2 CS folks to trial.
- Week 3–5: add publish flow + RBAC + audit logging. Enable engineer linking flow (manual mapping).
- Week 6–8: pilot with one product team, collect usage, measure metrics.

Risks & open questions:
- Safety false positives may block legitimate templates — need reviewer override UX and SLA for reviewer responses.
- Cost estimate accuracy: per-request cost is approximate; users may be misled. Add explicit estimator disclaimers.
- RBAC complexity: org policy may prevent self-publish for some teams. Need org-level feature flag.
- What counts as a template variable type & validation rules? (TODO: define schema for placeholders).
- Should templates be immutable after publish? likely no, but need clear rollback and deployment semantics.

Operational considerations:
- Sandbox quota for test runs per user per day (default 50 calls).
- Logging: store test-run inputs/outputs encrypted with retention policy; allow deletion for PII risk.
- Rollback path: when a template is rolled back, runtime should fallback to last published version; engineers must be notified via webhook.

Experiment ideas / quick hacks to validate demand:
- Quick Google Form + 1-hour office hours where PMs try a clickable prototype and we measure time-to-first-draft.
- Ship a simple Gmail-style prompt template email that non-devs can send to a special address to create a draft template (low-effort).

Notes to self / TODOs:
- Talk to SRE about retention/encryption for test-run logs (ticket: JIRA-REINF-459).
- Ask Safety team for scoring thresholds and override workflow (cc: amara.reed).
- Mock token estimator with 3 models (gpt-lite, gpt-standard, gpt-long) — get cost per token from billing team.
- Wire a Slack slash command /prompt-preview for quick testing (nice-to-have).

References / inspiration:
- notion: content templates + variables UX (good for non-devs).
- internal: route versioning model in Console (reuse ideas).
- external: copywriting tools like Jasper/Copy.ai for example-level UX patterns.

Questions for next sync with product/design:
- What is the minimum set of placeholder types we need to support? (string, enum, json?)
- Do we ship the safety classifier gate at launch or delay to reduce friction?
- Who will be the pilot org/team? recommendations: Search UX, Support Ops.

Bottom line: build an iterative, low-friction Prompt Studio that unlocks non-dev prompt ownership while keeping eng/infra in control. Start tiny (editor + test pane + publish with RBAC) and iterate based on real cross-functional usage.
